EU-ForDAM: cross-species correlation of insect damage

Step 1–7 summary — groundwork for gap-filling (no imputation done)

Published

October 8, 2026

Data and decisions

Source: EUForDam_REW3.xlsx, sheet EUForDam_REW: 30019 rows, 16 countries, 49 species codes, 77 regions, 2000–2022.

Processing decisions (agreed before analysis):

  • Damage variable = value1. value2 is filled for ~12% of rows; in most countries it is an exact constant fraction of value1 (a unit conversion), in DE a sub-part of it.
  • CZ sub-rows summed to NUTS2. CZ has 1–3 rows per NUTS2-year-species (sub-regions, probably kraje); damage in m³/ha is additive. CZ values are multiples of 1/7 (cause unknown; a constant factor does not affect within-series correlations).
  • Zeros are real (observed_zero). NA values and missing rows are not monitored. As a sensitivity check, “suspect zeros” (zeros in a country-species-year where no region of that country reports any damage, 4,880 cells) are dropped and correlations recomputed.
  • Aggregate codes kept as their own units (CambXyl_con&BB_con&BO, CambXyl_con&BB_con&SM, CambXyl_con&BO, CambXyl_con&MD, Def_dec, Def_dec&DB) and flagged. Their content differs between countries (e.g. CambXyl_con&BB_con&SM is the main spruce bark-beetle record in CZ but a minor residual group in DE).
  • Units are fixed per species (defoliators ha, borers m³), not per country. NUTS level differs by country (national for 11 countries, NUTS1 DE, NUTS2 AT/CZ/PL, NUTS3 FI), so raw log_damage levels are not comparable across countries; z_within, detrended and diff are.
  • “Impossible” (host absent) is a placeholder column (TODO: host-tree maps).

Coverage

Of 86,779 region-year-species cells, 11% are observed positive, 20% observed zero and 69% not monitored. DE reports 45 of 49 codes; most other countries report 1–21. ips_typ is the only species recorded by nearly every country.

DE dominates the observed data (74% of its cells are zeros), so pooled correlations lean heavily on DE.

Pairwise correlations (Step 4)

1008 of 1176 species pairs have an interpretable pooled z_within correlation (n ≥ 10 co-observed region-years). Strength of |r|: negligible 312, weak 483, moderate 171, strong 42.

version pairs median |r| pairs FDR < 0.05 share r > 0
detrended 1008 0.13 224 66%
diff 1064 0.05 164 61%
log_damage 1064 0.14 595 72%
z_within 1008 0.16 304 65%

diff gives the weakest correlations, as expected (year-to-year noise dominates). log_damage is shown for reference only. p-values are optimistic: years within a series are autocorrelated and region-years are not independent. Effect size, n and cross-country consistency are the main evidence.

Zero sensitivity. Dropping suspect zeros, pooled z_within r correlates 0.69 with the main run; 147 pairs lose their estimate. The strongest pairs barely move (see tables), but weak pairs are sensitive to how zeros are treated. The column n_both_positive counts region-years where both species had damage; pairs with few such years are driven mainly by shared zeros.

Temporal vs spatial (Step 5)

Temporal = pooled within-series z_within r; spatial = r between region means of log_damage across regions (co-observed years only). Linked = |r| ≥ 0.3.

linked_by pairs
neither 403
place 385
insufficient data 168
both 127
timing 76
timing (place untestable) 10
neither (place untestable) 7

Many pairs are linked “by place” only: regions with a lot of one species tend to have a lot of another, mainly because large regions (and whole countries reported nationally) have more damage of everything. Spatial links are therefore weak evidence for gap-filling; temporal links are the useful part.

Transferability across countries (Step 6) — most important

Flag rules (z_within, Pearson): consistent = ≥ 2 countries with n ≥ 10, every country r has the pooled sign, SD of country r ≤ 0.2, and no leave-one-country-out sign flip; inconsistent = ≥ 2 countries but a rule fails; insufficient data = < 2 countries.

transferability pairs
consistent 120
inconsistent 175
insufficient data 881

Most pairs (881) cannot be tested because only one country, usually DE, records both species. Transferability is the binding constraint for gap-filling.

These are mostly within the pine bark-borer complex (ips_sex, ips_acu, pha_cya, tom_spp, pis_pin, the pine borer aggregate) and the pine defoliators (bup_pin, pan_fla, den_pin), plus ips_typ × pit_spp across four countries. Some cross guild/host lines (agr_big on oak × pha_cya on pine, DE and PL) suggest shared drivers such as drought years. Two negative pairs involve pri_abi. Most “consistent” pairs rest on only 2 countries.

  • ips_typ × pit_cha is the strongest pooled pair (r = 0.65) and strong in DE and AT, but weak in LT/SK and negative in IT. National series (n ≈ 23) are much noisier than the regional DE/AT data.
  • Pairs with the CambXyl_con&BB_con&SM aggregate are strong in CZ and weak or negative in DE, which is consistent with that code meaning different things in the two countries.

Guild structure (Step 7)

Guild/host lookup used here: provisional (from file) (borer vs defoliator from the indicator columns; conifer vs broadleaf from TREETYPE). Fill in data/lookup/species_guild_TEMPLATE.csv, save it as data/lookup/species_guild.csv and rerun the pipeline to use your classification.

grouping version pairs within pairs between mean r within mean r between difference p (permutation)
guild z_within 521 487 0.13 0.04 0.09 0.0001
host z_within 547 461 0.09 0.08 0.01 0.2900
guild_host z_within 306 702 0.12 0.07 0.06 0.0055
guild detrended 521 487 0.09 0.04 0.05 0.0028
host detrended 547 461 0.07 0.06 0.01 0.1500
guild_host detrended 306 702 0.09 0.06 0.03 0.0380

Species do cluster by guild: same-guild pairs correlate more strongly than cross-guild pairs (permutation p ≤ 0.003 for both z_within and detrended, 9,999 label permutations, seed 20261008). Host type alone (conifer vs broadleaf) does not separate them. The clearest block is the bark-beetle complex on conifers (ips_typ, pit_cha, ips_cem, ips_sex, pha_cya, pit_bid, tom_spp, ips_acu). Within-guild differences are modest (mean r 0.13 vs 0.04).

Clustering caveat: 168 species pairs without an interpretable r were set to r = 0 for clustering only.

The matching n heatmap is outputs/figures/n_coobserved_heatmap.png.

Open questions

  1. Zeros vs not recorded. Results for weak pairs depend on this. Could the data compiler (or national contacts) confirm which countries record zeros explicitly, particularly LT, DE and the national series?
  2. What is value2 and why are CZ values multiples of 1/7?
  3. Aggregates. Should CZ CambXyl_con&BB_con&SM be treated as I. typographus for transfer purposes? It is the main source of inconsistent pairs.
  4. Guild/host lookup. The test above uses a provisional borer/defoliator split; bark vs wood borers need your table.
  5. Host-tree maps are needed for the “impossible” class.
  6. Few countries per pair. Transferability can be tested for only 295 pairs. For gap-filling, transfer from DE to other countries is mostly untested.
  7. Autocorrelation. If p-values matter later, a block bootstrap by region or a mixed model with year/region effects would give honest uncertainty.
